value: plants touched by a rotating paper arm for 10 days averaged 5.4 cm in height against 17.31 cm for untouched controls (unpaired t-test, P < 0.0001, t = 13.85, df = 22)
method: 12 clonal plants touched on the tops by a 40 cm rotating arm fitted with a paper sheet (3.3 rpm, 10 days) compared with 12 untouched control plants; plant height measured and compared by unpaired t-test
conditions: 24 clones from one parent plant (one genotype), n = 12 touched and 12 control; growth chamber at 21 C under constant light; touch force not stated; the same paper reports other endpoints (UdTCH1 expression about twofold higher in touched plants, UdERF4 and UdTCH4 about half of control, UdZFP2 no difference; stem anatomy from two biological replicates), and this record covers only the height comparison; growth reduction under repeated touch is a physiological endpoint, no touch receptor is identified

source.authors: Zajączkowska U, Dmitruk D, Sekulska-Nalewajko J, et al.
source.title: The impact of mechanical stress on anatomy, morphology, and gene expression in Urtica dioica L.

quote: We found a significant height difference (P < 0.0001, t = 13.85, df = 22), with the stimulated group averaging 5.4 cm and the control group 17.31 cm.
note: Thigmomorphogenesis in Urtica dioica; evidence_kind physiological_response because the endpoint is height under a touch versus untouched comparison. Single clonal genotype.
